content: {"rules": ["Model forecasts tend to overestimate prices in bullish event periods, especially when sentiment is positive.", "Forecast bias is amplified when official supply net is positive and sentiment is mixed or bearish.", "Sentiment spikes during high-event periods often trigger model overconfidence, leading to price overshoots.", "Model forecasts show mean-reversion bias in low-event periods with negative sentiment, underestimating sharp declines.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment aligns with supply net direction, particularly in high-event windows.", "Model lag is evident when true outcomes deviate sharply from forecasts during high-event periods with strong sentiment.", "Forecast bias is reduced when sentiment is consistently negative and supply net is negative, indicating market correction.", "Sentiment interaction with event supply net is critical — bullish sentiment without supply support leads to forecast overreach."]}
